```{r setup}
library(httr)
library(apastats2)
library(data.table)
library(jsonlite)
library(stringr)
library(knitr)
library(Hmisc)

default_font = 'Gill Sans Nova Light'

default_font_size <- 10
default_line_size <- 1/.pt/3.82*4 
default_font_size_mm <- default_font_size/ggplot2:::.pt

default_point_size <- 4*default_line_size

update_geom_defaults("line", list(linewidth = default_line_size))
update_geom_defaults("text", list(size = default_font_size_mm, family = default_font))
update_geom_defaults("segment", list(linewidth = default_line_size))
update_geom_defaults("pointrange", list(linewidth = default_line_size))
update_geom_defaults("vline", list(linewidth = default_line_size, colour = '#AFABAB'))
update_geom_defaults("hline", list(linewidth = default_line_size, colour = '#AFABAB'))

default_theme<-theme_light(base_size = default_font_size, base_line_size = default_line_size, base_family = default_font)+theme(
  axis.line=element_line(linewidth = I(0.5)), 
  axis.ticks= element_line(linewidth = I(0.25), colour = 'gray'),
  axis.line.x=element_line(),
  axis.line.y=element_line(),
  panel.grid.major = element_blank(), 
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  legend.title=element_text(size=rel(1)), 
  strip.text=element_text(size=rel(1), colour = 'black'), 
  axis.text=element_text(size=rel(0.9), colour = '#4e4e4e'), 
  axis.title=element_text(size=rel(1), colour = '#4e4e4e'), 
  panel.border= element_blank(),
  strip.background = element_blank(),

theme_set(default_theme)

default_colors <-c('#3498db','#009f06','#FF7F00', '#7A378B','#f72034')
decoy_colors <- c(competitor = default_colors[1], target = default_colors[2],
                  no_decoy = default_colors[3])
scale_colour_discrete <- function(...) scale_colour_manual(values=default_colors, ...)
scale_fill_discrete <- function(...) scale_fill_manual(values=default_colors, ...)

```

```{r}
#| label: data_prep

headers = c(
  `Authorization` = sprintf("Bearer %s", Sys.getenv("JATOS_TOKEN"))
)

jatos_url <- 'https://jatos.mindprobe.eu/jatos/api/v1/'

randstring <- function(n = 5000) {
  a <- do.call(paste0, replicate(5, sample(LETTERS, n, TRUE), FALSE))
  paste0(a, sprintf("%04d", sample(9999, n, TRUE)), sample(LETTERS, n, TRUE))
}

data_list <- list()
study_uid <- Sys.getenv('JATOS_DECOY_STUDY_2026H_UID')
study_version <- 'H26-shopping-240-v1'

temp_dir <- tempdir(check = T)
temp_dir <- gsub('\\\\', '/', temp_dir)
temp_dir <- paste(temp_dir, randstring(1), sep = '/')
res_file <- paste0(tempfile(),'.zip')

url <-  sprintf("%sresults?studyUuid=%s", jatos_url, study_uid)
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv('JATOS_TOKEN')) || !nzchar(study_uid)) {
  stop('Load the teaching project token and H26 study configuration before rendering.')
}
download <- GET(url, add_headers(.headers = headers), write_disk(res_file), handle = handle(''))
stop_for_status(download)
unzip(res_file, exdir=temp_dir)  # unzip your file

export_metadata <- jsonlite::fromJSON(list.files(temp_dir, '*.json', full.names = T, recursive = T))
if (!NROW(export_metadata$data) || !NROW(export_metadata$data$studyResults[[1]])) {
  stop('No study results are available for this report.')
}
metadata <- export_metadata$data$studyResults[[1]]

finished_study_ids <- metadata[metadata$studyState == 'FINISHED', c('id', 'endDate', 'startDate')]
setDT(finished_study_ids)
finished_study_ids[,id:=as.character(id)]
finished_study_ids[,endDate:=as.POSIXct(endDate/1000, origin="1970-01-01")]
finished_study_ids[,startDate:=as.POSIXct(startDate/1000, origin="1970-01-01")]
finished_study_ids <- finished_study_ids[startDate > Sys.getenv("JATOS_START_DATE") & !is.na(endDate)]
comp_res_meta <- rbindlist(lapply(1:length(metadata$componentResults), \(x) {
  dt <- as.data.table(metadata$componentResults[[x]])
  dt
}), fill = T)

flist <- list.files(temp_dir, '*.txt', full.names = T, recursive = T)
flist <- flist[str_extract(flist,'study_result_(\\d+)', group = 1)%in%finished_study_ids$id]

data <- suppressWarnings(rbindlist(lapply(c(flist), \(x){
  print(x)
  comp_res_id <- str_extract(x, '(?<=comp-result_)\\d{6}')
  data <- read_json(x)
  if (length(data)<10){
    return(data.frame())
  }
  data <- data[sapply(data, \(x) x$trial_type=='psychophysics')]
  data <- rbindlist(data, fill = T)
  data <- data[phase == 'main']  # drop the practice trials

  data[,subject_id:=str_extract(x, 'study_result_(\\d+)', group = 1)]
  data[,result_id:=str_extract(x, 'comp-result_(\\d+)', group = 1)]
  data <- merge(data, finished_study_ids, by.x = 'subject_id', by.y = 'id')
  
  data
  
}), fill = T))

unlink(paste0(temp_dir, "/*"))

if (!nrow(data) || !'exp_version' %in% names(data)) {
  stop('No results for the revised H26 protocol. Use the report matching your data version.')
}
data <- data[exp_version == study_version & !qa_mode]
if (!nrow(data)) stop('No finished human results for H26-shopping-240-v1.')
stopifnot(all(data[, .N, by = subject_id]$N == 240))

subject_ids <- sample(unique(data$subject_id))
data[, participant := match(subject_id, subject_ids)]
data[, c('startDate', 'endDate', 'result_id', 'subject_id', 'avg_frame_time') := NULL]

```

```{r}
data_timeouts <- data[, .(unanswered = sum(is.na(response)), total = .N),
                      by = .(participant, condition, decoy_on)]
data_out <- data[!is.na(response), .(participant, exp_version, trial_counter, round,
  chapter, condition, target_to_competitor, decoy_type, decoy_reduction, decoy_on,
  chosen_item, correct, rt = rt / 1000)][order(participant, trial_counter)]
stopifnot(data_out[, all(correct == (chosen_item == 'target'))])
fwrite(data_out, 'decoy_2026H.csv')

```

## Instructions

Read the report below and use it as a basis for your presentation. You can also download the preprocessed data from `decoy_2026H.csv` and use your favorite software (JASP, jamovi, R, SPSS) to analyze it to get more insight into the study results. The data file has the following columns:

This report selects finished human sessions from `H26-shopping-240-v1`.
Earlier H26 revisions and local QA bots are excluded. The CSV contains answered
main trials; practice, unanswered trials, and debrief interactions are excluded.

* `participant` - random participant ID
* `exp_version` - protocol version
* `trial_counter` - main-trial number (1–240; gaps identify unanswered trials)
* `round`, `chapter` - shopping round (1–15) and chapter (1–3)
* `condition` [`numeric`/`perceptual`] - bars with prices/ratings, or bars alone
* `target_to_competitor` [0.03/0.10] - reduction of one competitor bar on the full bar scale
* `decoy_type` [`stronger`/`weaker`/`both`] - which bar(s) of the attached option were reduced
* `decoy_reduction` [0.05/0.20] - total bar reduction; split equally when type is `both`
* `decoy_on` [`target`/`competitor`/`no_decoy`] - decoy placement, including two-option controls
* `chosen_item` [`target`/`competitor`/`decoy`] - selected offer
* `correct` - task score (1 for a target choice, 0 for another offer)
* `rt` - seconds from stimulus/response-window onset to the response

Decoy type and reduction are missing in controls because there is no decoy.
Do not remove control trials by excluding rows with missing values in these
columns. Analyze those two factors only within the decoy trials.

## Method

### Participants
`r data_out[,xfun::numbers_to_words(lengthu(participant))]` participants  were recruited to take part in an online experiment and responded with a keyboard. Demographic information was not collected.

{{< include decoy_choices_methods_2026H.md >}}

## Descriptive statistics

```{r descr_stats}
data_descr <- data_out[, .(n = .N, mean_RT = mean(rt)),
                       by = .(participant, decoy_present = decoy_on != 'no_decoy', chosen_item)]
choice_grid <- unique(data_descr[, .(participant, decoy_present)])[,
  .(chosen_item = if (decoy_present) c('target', 'competitor', 'decoy') else c('target', 'competitor')),
  by = .(participant, decoy_present)]
data_descr <- merge(choice_grid, data_descr, all.x = TRUE)
data_descr[is.na(n), n := 0]
data_descr[, prop_choices := 100 * n / sum(n), by = .(participant, decoy_present)]
```

On average, participants chose `r data_descr[decoy_present==T,apa_mean_conf(prop_choices), by = .(chosen_item)][,paste_and(sprintf('%ss in %s', chosen_item, V1))]`% of trials (here and later the confidence intervals are reported in square brackets after the means) when a decoy was present.  Response times were `r data_descr[decoy_present == TRUE & !is.na(mean_RT), apa_mean_conf(mean_RT), by = .(chosen_item)][,paste_and(V1)]`, respectively. When the decoy was absent, participants chose `r data_descr[decoy_present==F,apa_mean_conf(prop_choices), by = .(chosen_item)][,paste_and(sprintf('%ss in %s', chosen_item, V1))]`% of trials with response times of `r data_descr[decoy_present == FALSE & !is.na(mean_RT), apa_mean_conf(mean_RT), by = .(chosen_item)][,paste_and(V1)]`.

Across main trials, `r sum(data_timeouts$unanswered)` of `r sum(data_timeouts$total)`
were unanswered. Choice percentages exclude these trials; response-time means
include only recorded responses. RT summaries for an option include only the
participants who selected that option.

## Do decoys influence choices differently under different conditions?

```{r}
#| fig-cap: Mean participant choice percentages by presentation and decoy placement. Percentages account for unequal trial counts; unanswered trials are excluded.
#| label: fig-resp_count
choice_counts <- data_out[, .(n = .N), by = .(participant, condition, decoy_on, chosen_item)]
choice_grid <- unique(choice_counts[, .(participant, condition, decoy_on)])[,
  .(chosen_item = if (decoy_on == 'no_decoy') c('target', 'competitor') else c('target', 'competitor', 'decoy')),
  by = .(participant, condition, decoy_on)]
choice_props <- merge(choice_grid, choice_counts, all.x = TRUE)
choice_props[is.na(n), n := 0]
choice_props[, prop_choices := 100 * n / sum(n), by = .(participant, condition, decoy_on)]
choice_plot <- choice_props[, .(prop_choices = mean(prop_choices)), by = .(condition, decoy_on, chosen_item)]
ggplot(choice_plot, aes(x = chosen_item, y = prop_choices, fill = decoy_on)) +
  geom_col(position = 'dodge') + facet_grid(~condition) +
  labs(y = 'Mean participant choice percentage', fill = 'Choice set', x = 'Chosen option') +
  scale_fill_manual(values = decoy_colors, breaks = names(decoy_colors))
```

@fig-resp_count shows the relationship between the decoy placement (target, competitor, or no decoy), condition (whether there were numeric labels present [numeric] or not [perceptual]), and the probability of choosing one of the response options.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: The effects of decoy placement and condition on the accuracy of observers' responses.
#| label: fig-accuracy

res <- ez::ezANOVA(data_out, dv = 'correct', within = c('condition','decoy_on'), wid = .(participant), type = 3)

plot_pointrange(data_out, aes(x = condition, y = correct, color = decoy_on), wid = 'participant', design = 'w', within_subj =  T)+labs(y = 'Proportion of correct responses', color = 'Choice set', x = 'Condition')+scale_color_manual(values = decoy_colors, breaks = names(decoy_colors))
```

The effects of decoy placement and condition were then analyzed using a within-subject ANOVA with response accuracy (correct or not; correct here means that a target is chosen) as a dependent variable (@fig-accuracy). The results are provided below:

* the effect of condition `r apa(res, 'condition')`
* the effect of decoy placement `r apa(res, 'decoy_on')`
* the effect of their interaction `r apa(res, 'condition:decoy_on')`


```{r}
#| fig-cap: The effects of decoy placement and condition on the observers' response times.
#| label: fig-rt

res_rt <- ez::ezANOVA(data_out, dv = 'rt', within = c('condition','decoy_on'), wid = .(participant), type = 3)

plot_pointrange(data_out, aes(x = condition, y = rt, color = decoy_on), wid = 'participant', design = 'w', within_subj = T)+labs(y = 'Response time, s', color = 'Choice set', x = 'Condition')+scale_color_manual(values = decoy_colors, breaks = names(decoy_colors))
```

Lastly, we analyzed the response times again using a within-subject ANOVA (@fig-rt). The results are provided below:

* the effect of condition `r apa(res_rt, 'condition')`
* the effect of decoy placement `r apa(res_rt, 'decoy_on')`
* the effect of their interaction `r apa(res_rt, 'condition:decoy_on')`
